text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller plans to order high ranking generals into retirement when she becomes prime minister under coalition powersharing deal.
- A tender of $250 million to build another terminal at Istanbul airport is deadlocked.
MILLIYET
- Aide to conservative Ciller says there is no point in revamping the current coalition with Islamists.
HURRIYET
- Conservative main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz calls on Ciller's True Path Party to cooperate with it.
- Yonca sunflower and corn oil producer builds $10-million factory in western town of Manisa.
YENI YUZYIL
- The Developing-8 (D-8) alliance between eight Moslem states comes into being at summit in Istanbul.
- Troops kill 58 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) militants in eastern Turkey.
RADIKAL
- The ball will be in President Suleyman Demirel's court after Wednesday, when Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan is expected to resign.
- General manager of Disbank Bank Halil Eroglu says the markets are already indexed to early elections. Eroglu says inflation rate will soar if polls are held in October.
CUMHURIYET
- Plans to crack down on Islamist education in line with army demands have been shelved by the government.
DUNYA
- Government business grounds to a halt as political uncertainty dominates.
ZAMAN
- Authorities in western coastal province of Izmir give Father's Day dinner for the fathers of those who lost their lives in the fight against the PKK.
